questions.question: The normal gestational period (full term) is:
questions.explanation: A normal pregnancy lasts about 37-42 weeks, averaging 40.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The normal span of pregnancy is about:
questions.explanation: A full-term pregnancy is about 40 weeks (280 days) from the last menstrual period.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The weight gain seen in the first trimester is usually about:
questions.explanation: Weight gain is small, about 1-2 kg, in the first trimester.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: There is an associated risk of ______ if weight gain during pregnancy is less than 5 kg.
questions.explanation: Poor maternal weight gain restricts fetal growth.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: At the end of the first trimester, the fetus is about ______ in length.
questions.explanation: The crown-rump length at 12 weeks is about 6-7 cm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: During labour, the cervix dilates to nearly:
questions.explanation: Full dilatation is 10 cm, at which the fetal head can pass.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following statements about pulmonary changes in pregnancy is FALSE?

options.A: The diaphragm rises by about 4 cm
options.B: The AP and transverse chest diameters each increase by about 2 cm
options.D: The chest circumference increases by 5-7 cm

questions.explanation: The subcostal angle widens in pregnancy as the lower ribs flare.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: During pregnancy, the increase in blood volume is about:
questions.explanation: Blood volume rises 35-50 percent, peaking at about 32-34 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In late pregnancy, which position can cause symptomatic supine hypotension?
questions.explanation: The gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava in supine, reducing venous return.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Side lying is advised for pregnant women because it:

options.C: Reduces IVC compression caused in the supine position

questions.explanation: Left lateral position relieves aortocaval compression.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In pregnancy, the centre of gravity shifts:
questions.explanation: The growing uterus moves the COG forward and upward.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Postural backache in pregnancy is due to:
questions.explanation: The forward shift of the COG increases lumbar lordosis and strains the back.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which hormone is responsible for ligament laxity in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Relaxin (with progesterone) softens ligaments and the pubic symphysis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The hormone relaxin released during pregnancy most frequently affects the ______ joints.
questions.explanation: Sacroiliac laxity causes pelvic girdle pain in pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pregnancy-related syndrome?
questions.explanation: Symphysis diastasis, SI dysfunction and varicose veins are common in pregnancy; lymphoedema is not.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In an anthropoid pelvis the ______ diameter is long.
questions.explanation: An anthropoid pelvis has a long AP and short transverse diameter.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When a perineal laceration includes only skin, it is classified as:
questions.explanation: First-degree tears involve perineal skin and vaginal mucosa only.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When a perineal laceration includes skin and the underlying perineal muscle, it is classified as:
questions.explanation: Second-degree tears involve the perineal muscles but not the anal sphincter.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When a perineal laceration extends to the anal sphincter, it is classified as:
questions.explanation: Third-degree tears involve the anal sphincter complex.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the rectal mucosa is lacerated, the perineal laceration is classified as:
questions.explanation: Fourth-degree tears extend through the anal sphincter into the rectal mucosa.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Diastasis recti is diagnosed when the separation between the rectus abdominis muscles is larger than about:
questions.explanation: An inter-rectus distance above about 2 cm (2 finger-widths) is considered a diastasis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to exercise in pregnant women?
questions.explanation: Significant heart disease, pre-eclampsia, persistent bleeding and ruptured membranes contraindicate exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: On the first day after lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) the physiotherapy programme should comprise:

options.B: Breathing, coughing and pelvic floor exercises

questions.explanation: Early postoperative exercise prevents chest complications and restores circulation and pelvic floor function.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which contractions increase circulation to the uterus and baby and are experienced in the third trimester by the pregnant woman?
questions.explanation: Painless irregular uterine contractions that become more frequent as term approaches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A primigravida normally first feels the movements of the foetus (quickening) at about:
questions.explanation: Quickening occurs at about 18-20 weeks in a first pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the bladder herniates into the vagina, it is termed:
questions.explanation: A cystocele is anterior vaginal wall prolapse with the bladder.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the rectum herniates into the vagina, it is termed:
questions.explanation: A rectocele is a bulge of the posterior vaginal wall.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: When the uterus bulges into the vagina, it is termed:
questions.explanation: Uterine descent into the vagina is uterovaginal prolapse.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is a contributing factor for stress incontinence?

options.C: Pelvic floor muscle weakness, together with coughing and laughing

questions.explanation: Raised intra-abdominal pressure leaks urine when the pelvic floor is weak.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
